newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Bre-X, Barrick deal seen this week-source.
newsitem.headline: Bre-X, Barrick deal seen this week-source.

text.p: Canada's Bre-X Minerals Ltd and Barrick Gold Corp are expected to strike a deal by the end of the week on jointly developing Indonesia's huge Busang gold find, a source close to the negotiations said on Wednesday.
"I expect things to be in place by the end of this week," the source told Reuters. "We are expected to settle the negotiations by this week."
The source declined to give further details, saying he was bound by a confidentiality pact signed by Bre-X and Barrick.

Bre-X chairman and chief executive officer David Walsh said that the Indonesian government had given Bre-X and Barrick until February 14 to reach an agreement with their respective local partners over the Busang property in East Kalimantan province.
Bre-X estimates the property contains at least 57 million ounces of gold worth over $21 billion at current prices.

Indonesia said last November it wanted Bre-X to partner Barrick, and the Mines and Energy Ministry said in December they had agreed to split Busang, with 22.5 percent going to Bre-X, 67.5 percent to Barrick and the rest to the government.

Indonesia's Nusamba group, 80 percent owned by three foundations headed by President Suharto and 10 percent each by timber baron Muhammad "Bob" Hasan and Suharto's eldest son Sigit Harjojudanto, has bought a 50-percent stake in two companies with minority interests in two of the Busang areas.
Barrick has an alliance with a company controlled by Suharto's eldest daughter Siti Hardijanti Rukmana.
State-controlled tin miner PT Tambang Timah has said it was holding talks with Hasan over an equity participation in Busang.
